title: Nifty slips for seventh day as crude surge, bond yield spike rattle markets - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
On the sectoral performance from Tuesday’s session, the Defence index gained 1.30 per cent, while IT shed 1.90 per cent. Auto, Media and Oil & Gas ended in positive territory, while FMCG, Realty and Metal closed between 0.6 per cent and 1.9 per cent lower. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Markets opened flat to marginally negative on Wednesday, extending a six-session losing streak, as rising crude oil prices and surging global bond yields kept investor sentiment under pressure.

The Nifty 50 opened at 24,152.05, against its previous close of 24,154.90, and was trading at 24,114.00, down 40.90 points or 0.17 per cent, as of 9.17 AM. The Sensex opened at 77,218.05 against its previous close of 77,235.46, and was quoting at 77,127.18, down 108.28 points or 0.14 per cent.

IT stocks led the gainers in early trade. HCL Technologies rose 1.51 per cent to ₹1,317.60, while Infosys gained 1.46 per cent to ₹1,131.30. Eternal added 0.79 per cent to ₹318.40, Wipro edged up 0.62 per cent to ₹179.17, and Tech Mahindra was up 0.59 per cent at ₹1,601.40.

On the losing side, Hindalco fell 1.31 per cent to ₹1,028.00, while Bajaj Finserv dropped 1.24 per cent to ₹1,986.30. Tata Steel declined 1.18 per cent to ₹183.31 and Bajaj Finance lost an equal 1.18 per cent, trading at ₹1,081.40. SBI Life Insurance fell 1.09 per cent to ₹1,758.60.

The broader market context remains challenging. "The ongoing mild weakness in the market is driven mainly by two factors: one, the rising crude prices, and two, appreciating bond yields globally," said Dr. VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. "Crude prices are rising anticipating the continuation of the uncertainty. Fears of rising inflation are pushing bond yields higher."

The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield has climbed to its highest level since 2007, approaching 5.33 per cent–5.34 per cent intraday, driven by widening fiscal deficits, inflation concerns, and heavy capital demand from debt-financed AI infrastructure. Bond yields are also rising in Japan, where the 10-year government bond yield is approaching 3 per cent, a three-decade high, and in Germany, adding to the global pressure on equities.

Brent crude has crossed $91 per barrel after the 60-day U.S.-Iran ceasefire expired without a new agreement, with Iran shifting to what it described as a "fully offensive" military posture and fresh attacks reported in the Strait of Hormuz. WTI crude is trading in the $84–85 per barrel range. India's crude oil import bill rose 41 per cent year-on-year to $13.7 billion in July, with volumes climbing 13 per cent to 21.4 million tonnes.

Wall Street closed lower for a third consecutive session on Tuesday. The Nasdaq fell 1.33 per cent, the S&P 500 dropped 0.69 per cent, and the Dow Jones slipped 0.22 per cent. The semiconductor index tumbled around 5.5 per cent. Asian markets followed suit, with Japan's Nikkei 225 falling over 2 per cent and South Korea's Kospi dropping more than 4 per cent.

On the sectoral performance from Tuesday's session, the Defence index gained 1.30 per cent, while IT shed 1.90 per cent. Auto, Media and Oil & Gas ended in positive territory, while FMCG, Realty and Metal closed between 0.6 per cent and 1.9 per cent lower.

Technically, the Nifty closed below the key 24,200 cluster support on Tuesday. "As long as the market is trading below 24,200/77,300, a weak sentiment is likely to continue," said Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Securities. "The market is likely to retest the levels of 24,050–24,000/77,000–76,700."

Despite the weakness, institutional flows have provided some support. Foreign Institutional Investors turned net buyers on Tuesday, purchasing equities worth ₹1,651 crore. Domestic Institutional Investors extended their buying streak to a sixth consecutive session, investing ₹2,579 crore.

The rupee weakened 8 paise to close at ₹95.68 per dollar on Tuesday, pressured by higher crude prices and weak domestic equities.

Gold eased below $4,400 as higher U.S. yields and safe-haven dollar demand offset support from Middle East risk.

"Long-term investors can use the ongoing weakness in the market to accumulate quality growth stocks," said Dr. Vijayakumar. "The prospects for GDP growth and earnings growth for FY27 are improving, and this along with abundant domestic liquidity is keeping the market resilient."

Markets will closely watch the minutes of the U.S. Federal Reserve's July policy meeting, due later today, for signals on the interest rate trajectory. Any shift in the Fed's outlook could significantly influence Treasury yields, the dollar and capital flows into emerging markets including India.
